$$ = {{p(1)} \over {(1 - p){1 \over 5} + p(1)}} = {p \over {{{1 - p + 5p} \over 5}}} = {{5p} \over {1 + 4p}}$$

en.content: A bar magnet is oscillating in the earth's magnetic field with a period T. What happens to its period and motion, if its mass is quadrupled?

options.content: Motion remains simple harmonic with time period 4T.
Motion remains simple harmonic with time period nearly constant.
Motion remains simple harmonic and time period becomes T/2.
Motion remains simple harmonic with time period 2T.

en.explanation:
Time period of simple harmonic motion,

$$T = 2\pi \sqrt {\left| {{\theta \over \alpha }} \right|} = 2\pi \sqrt {{1 \over {mH}}} $$

$$ \Rightarrow T \propto \sqrt I \Rightarrow T \propto \sqrt m $$ [$$\therefore$$ $$I = {{m{l^2}} \over {12}}$$]

$${{{T_1}} \over {{T_2}}} = \sqrt {{{{m_1}} \over {{m_2}}}} = \sqrt {{m \over {4m}}} = {1 \over 2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {T_2} = 2{T_1} = 2T$$ [$$\therefore$$ $${T_1} = T$$]

so, motion remains simple harmonic with time period 2T.

en.explanation:

Carnot cycle of an engine is given below

Total work done by the gas in one cycle is
en.explanation:
Total work done by the gas

$${W_{Total}} = {W_{P \to Q}} + {W_{Q \to R}} + {W_{R \to S}} + {W_{S \to P}}$$

Work done in isothermal process by ideal gas

$${W_{P \to Q}} = \mu RT_1\log {{{V_2}} \over {{V_1}}}$$ ..... (i)

Work done in adiabatic process by ideal gas

$${W_{Q \to R}} = {{ \mu R({T_1} - {T_2})} \over {r - 1}}$$ ..... (ii)

Work done in isothermal process by ideal gas,

$${W_{R \to S}} = - \mu R{T_2}\log {{{V_3}} \over {{V_4}}}$$ ...... (iii)

Work done in adiabatic process, by ideal gas

$${W_{S \to P}} = {{ - \mu R({T_1} - {T_2})} \over {r - 1}}$$ ..... (iv)

Adding Eqs. (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) we get

$${W_{Total}} = \mu R{T_1}\log {{{V_2}} \over {{V_1}}} - \mu R{T_2}\log {{{V_3}} \over {{V_4}}}$$
